claims: Every statement on docs/explanation/ossie.md, docs/how-to/share-an-ossie-ontology.md, docs/how-to/describe-delivered-tables-for-ossie.md, the Ossie section of src/gnd/skills/gnd-export/SKILL.md and the release-note section is true of the code at this commit; check each against the source and the normative sections, and name any that is false, overstated or stated nowhere normative.

The pages state no rule of their own: every rule id, reason, limit and exit code they mention is stated in the normative sections, with the same meaning. Look for a rule said twice in different words that could drift.

tests/test_ossie_docs.py can fail: a page naming an unknown binding: or ossie: id, an Ossie flag missing from the skill, the CLI reference or the normative section, or a wrong exit number in the release note each fail it. Read each new regular expression and string test there as a claim about its input class, build a legal input the tests lack, and report a wrong result.

is_regular_identifier and _quoted in src/gnd/export/ossie_relational.py write, for every table or column name a model or a schema-valid binding can produce, the identifier Ossie's validator normalizes the declared name to: uppercased for a regular identifier, as written otherwise. The independent restatement normalized() in tests/support/ossie_relational_corpus.py agrees with it on every name. Build names the tests lack (empty, one character, mixed scripts, case-changing-length characters, keywords in other cases) and report any disagreement.

The quoting fix changes no output for a name that is a regular identifier, so every OB2, OB3 and OB4 corpus answer except physical_binding/V2/expected.mapping.yaml and the census baselines are unchanged, and binding:name-collision still refuses every pair of names the exporter would write as one identifier.

The packaged example src/gnd/examples/refunds/physical-binding.json is a correct binding of the refunds model, the how-to describes it truthfully, and no public text names a downstream project, customer or reporter.
